title: Analytics permission middleware + query-level filtering for console usage APIs
text:
Analytics permission middleware + query-level filtering for console usage APIs

description:
Problem: Console analytics endpoints and pre-aggregated usage views currently expose broader tenant-scoped data than permissible for some roles. We need a backend enforcement layer to ensure only authorized principals can access sensitive dimensions (token_id, raw_user_id, full_request_body) and to enforce org/project/team isolation across both the API and the analytics pipeline outputs.

Goal: Implement a permissions middleware in the console backend plus query-level filters and pipeline-side row-level security so that analytics endpoints (live and pre-aggregated) return only authorized rows/columns. Ensure minimal latency impact for common queries and a safe rollout path for dedicated/private customers.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Console API returns 403 for attempts to access restricted dimensions by a principal without permission.
2) Pre-aggregated daily and hourly tables include tenant_id/project_id tags and are filtered during ingestion to exclude rows outside an org's scope.
3) Middleware integrates with existing SSO/roles mapping and respects group-level overrides from Dedicated customers.
4) No change in 95th percentile query latency > 15% for standard usage dashboards in canary.
5) Unit+integration tests cover role matrix and column-redaction rules.

tasks:
Design RBAC schema for analytics (roles -> allowed dimensions + row scope)
Implement Express middleware: resolve principal -> allowed scopes/dimensions
Add SQL query builder hooks to append WHERE clauses for row-level filtering
Add column-masking logic in API layer for sensitive columns when not permitted
Pipeline change: tag incoming events with org/project metadata and add ingestion-time filter step
Create migration plan for existing aggregated tables (backfill or rebuild)
Load tests + canary rollout + dashboards to monitor 403/500 rates and latency

notes:
Design tradeoffs considered:
- Option A: Enforce only at API layer (fast rollout) but risk bypass if other consumers query raw tables.
- Option B: Enforce at ingestion (stronger, single source) but requires backfill and more complex pipeline work.
We will implement a hybrid: API-level middleware for immediate protection + ingestion-time RLS for long-term guarantees.

Sensitive columns: token_id, raw_user_id, request_body. For Dedicated customers we will allow org-admin role to opt-in to more granular views via explicit contract and config flag.

Performance mitigation: push down filters to the materialized views and use precomputed tenant_id shards to limit scanned partitions. Cache permission decisions per principal for 60s to reduce auth backend calls.

Migration: create tenant-scoped copies of daily/hourly aggregates under analytics_v2.*, run parallel writes for 4 weeks, compare diffs on canary tenants, then switch reads.

implementation_notes:
- Use existing auth service endpoint /auth/principal -> {roles,orgs,projects} and cache results in-memory keyed by access_token hash.
- SQL injection protection: enforce prepared statements and validate injected WHERE fragments against allowlist of columns.
- Column redaction: implement per-field serializers that return null or pseudonymized id for disallowed fields.
- Telemetry: emit telemetry event analytics.authz.check with fields {principal,endpoint,allowed_dims,decision} - redact principal.id in logs.

rollout_plan:
1) Deploy middleware to staging and run smoke checks. 2) Enable API-level enforcement for 5% of production traffic (canary tenants). 3) Run differential checks between analytics_v2 and analytics_v1 for canary tenants for 14 days. 4) Enable ingestion-time filtering for all new partitions and run backfill for last 90 days. 5) Flip read path to analytics_v2 for all tenants. 6) Monitor errors/403s for 7 days before deprecating v1.

monitoring_sla_metrics:
- 403 rate by endpoint and tenant (alert if > baseline + 5%); - Query latency p50/p95 for analytics endpoints; - Ratio of quarantined events during ingestion; - Permission cache hit rate; - Number of redacted columns per query.

open_risks:
- Backfill cost: full rebuild of 180 days of aggregates estimated at ~1200 GPU-hours for aggregator jobs; need cost approval.
- SDKs sending incomplete metadata may prolong quarantine period.
- Dedicated customers with custom RBAC will require config-driven overrides and extra QA cycles.

next_steps:
1) Finalize RBAC schema and publish to Confluence (owner: Aisha). 2) Complete pipeline tagging PR and release to staging (owner: Priya). 3) Complete middleware integration tests and security review (owner: Marco).

review_feedback:
PM (Keisha Wong): Ensure grouping by project_id is compatible with billing view — add a mapping table if necessary.
Security (Daniel Roy): Request explicit threat model for token_id leakage and confirm KMS usage for token references.
Data Eng (Priya Menon): Prefer ingestion-time filtering for high-cardinality user_id to reduce downstream masking work.

comments:
2026-02-16 Marco Alvarez: Initial spike completed. Confirmed existing API returns unfiltered rows for /analytics/raw/events. Found missing project_id tag in 4% of events from older SDKs.
2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Added migration plan draft to Confluence and created analytics_v2 schema. Assigned data eng tasks to Priya.
2026-02-25 Priya Menon: Pipeline patching PR opened to add project_id tagging and drop events without a validated org mapping (PR infra#2120). If missing tags are >0.1% we'll route to quarantine topic for manual resolution.
2026-02-28 Security review queued with Security team — Daniel asked for encryption-at-rest confirmation for intermediate staging tables.
2026-03-01 Marco Alvarez: Middleware prototype merged to feature branch. Needs integration tests for role matrix and integration with SSO mapping endpoint.
